answer: Decaying identity bonds stop forgery at the wharf where agents dock. Each applicant locks a bond equal to twice its 30-day earnings, listed in an atlas. The bond loses 5% per epoch and vanishes after 20 epochs unless honest work renews it. Making 100 fakes costs 100 bonds, and decay bleeds idle fakes faster than rewards repay them. An honest agent pays once, renews by work, and keeps undiluted rewards: the kernel rule is that time taxes idleness.
